publications.title: Music’s Influence on Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, and Stress Levels in Working Adults
publications.subtitle: SSRG International Journal of Humanities and Social Science, Innosphere’23; Sigma Xi Conference (Sep 2023)
publications.description: Independent research on the relationship between music exposure and physiological stress indicators (heart rate, blood pressure). Presented findings at Innosphere’23 and Sigma Xi Conference; informed follow-up work on an AI-assisted music therapy prototype (Heartune). Explored the impact of various technical aspects of music on heart rate variability, blood pressure, and stress levels. I specifically examined factors such as the song's beats per minute (BPM), which determines the tempo, and considered the influence of time of day and the individual's mental state. By analyzing these variables, I aimed to uncover how different musical characteristics can affect physiological responses and overall stress levels in individuals.

projects.title: ChillTrill: Real-time Facial Expression Detection
projects.description: Built a real-time facial expression classification prototype using Python, OpenCV (face detection), and a CNN-based classifier deployed via Streamlit WebRTC. Achieved F1 = 0.81 on ~1,200 labeled clips and optimized inference to ~55 ms/frame for interactive performance. Developed an evaluation pipeline (error analysis across lighting/occlusion/pose), iterated on preprocessing + model architecture, and packaged reproducible experiments with versioned configs and clear documentation. Deployed a pilot to 3 partner institutions and incorporated user feedback into a roadmap for next iterations (improved UX, calibration, and model robustness).Tech/Tools: Python, OpenCV, Streamlit, WebRTC, deep learning, model evaluation, Githttps://chilltrill.streamlit.app/https://github.com/Saksham9426/ChillTrill

projects.title: Heartune: AI-assisted Music Therapy App + Research
projects.description: Developed an AI-assisted music therapy app prototype focused on personalization and measurable well-being outcomes. Built backend integration via REST APIs and implemented ML components for personalization and classification (e.g., kNN / Keras / TensorFlow prototypes depending on experiment), with an emphasis on evaluation and iterative improvement. Conducted independent research on the relationship between music and physiological stress signals; published and presented findings, including “Music’s Influence on Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, and Stress Levels in Working Adults” (presented at Innosphere’23 and the Sigma Xi Conference, Sep 2023). Received national media coverage (Times of India) and incorporated learnings into product iteration and research communication.Tech/Tools: Python, REST APIs, Keras, TensorFlow, kNN, experimentation, data analysis

We hosted the official YC afterparty for Startup School this year. More than 1000 people registered, but we could only fit about 200 in the room. After a day that big and that packed, we wanted something low-key. So we got a venue by the water, a DJ, and a couple hundred builders who wanted to keep the conversations going without the conference-hall energy. Spent four hours chit-chatting with students, developers, and future founders without any agenda. It's genuinely one of the best ways to meet the next wave of people building amazing things. Two years ago, we were the ones showing up to someone else's afterparty, asking founders for advice. Hosting our own this year felt like closing a loop. The reason afterparties are such big hits is that some of the most memorable conversations from events like this happen only after everyone's decompressed a bit.
YC delayed Startup School Day 2 for the SF marathon... so why not do both? :)

sf was a reminder that the best stuff is built in person. so i went. i spent the last week at Y Combinator startup school events, hosting and attending, with some of the most talented builders i’ve met. average age of startup school? 18-20. where was everyone at? Corgi cafe. youngest intern @ GitHub ? 16. here’s the sauce: • jachacks at Founders, Inc. , inc: helped throw a hackathon with Jaseci Labs . builders from stanford, mit, and berkeley shipping with support from NVIDIA and Google DeepMind . building near the shore was something i've never done. • internapalooza with Cory Levy : joined 20,000+ technical interns and founders of companies like Etched , Whop , and Cal AI . with speakers like sam altman @ OpenAI and Zach Yadegari ,. loved talking to him backstage. Z Fellows lesson: all it takes is one hope. • Google DeepMind 's yc event: met Ruoyu Zhang and David Dai . highlight of the day: comparing google's ai race with current day space-tech. • Mintlify + LemonLime + Respan : shoutout to the mintlify team ( Justin Torre and Marco Dewey ) for putting together a high-caliber event. met great people in deep-tech and agriculture. appreciated Jordan Zietz as well for throwing at the office, and swung by fav uiuc alum Andy Li and Frank Chen at the pearl. scary that tech is only becoming younger. but more than events, sometimes you got to lock yourself in a room, stop networking, and start creating - Darsh Poddar @ Autumn AI (YC W26) all love to Shivam Sharma + Lakshan Veer Abimanyu Ramakrishnamoorthy :) if we met and you want to chat, let’s keep the conversation going. daily reminder: altman at the age 19 had an interview with a top ceo and but was too young to rent a car. what can you do without a car? back to hustling 🦾 🏃‍♂️ #ycstartupschool #ycombinator #sanfrancisco #zfellows

After an extraordinarily fulfilling and unforgettable 21+ year journey with Accenture, today marks my last day. When I first joined the firm after returning from New Zealand back in 2005 (with a much younger version of myself on that first badge!), I could never have imagined how deeply Accenture would grow on me. Looking back over more than two decades, it has been a jolly good ride—always filled with passion, purpose, and energy. From building practices, driving large client transformations, and serving alongside world-class leaders on the India Market Unit Executive Committee and Global Leadership Council, every phase of this adventure has been deeply rewarding. Yet, when I look back, what I will cherish most isn't the business metrics or the scale—it is the incredible people I’ve had the privilege to work with across India, regional, and global ecosystems. To the senior leaders who provided invaluable guidance, mentorship, and strategic backing; to our clients who trusted us with their most critical challenges; and to my phenomenal colleagues and teammates who shared the trenches with me: thank you. Thank you for your trust, guidance, and the deep camaraderie that made navigating complex challenges so incredibly rewarding. Accenture will always hold a special place in my heart, and I leave with immense pride in everything we built together and full confidence in the firm’s future. I’m excited and look forward to stepping into my next professional chapter. More details on what’s ahead soon! To everyone who has been part of this 21-year story—thank you from the bottom of my heart. Please do stay in touch.
